step.body: We audit your data volume, query latency needs, and budget. We also test your documents against a long context model to measure baseline accuracy and cost per query.
A written architecture spec comparing RAG vs long context for your use case, including projected token costs, retrieval accuracy trade-offs, and freshness requirements—delivered within 48 hours.

We build a proof-of-concept for both approaches using your real data. For RAG, we set up a retrieval pipeline with chunking and embedding. For long context, we prefill the prompt with your corpus and measure latency.
We run side-by-side evaluations on accuracy, cost per query (including input tokens), and freshness. We use RAGAS for RAG and custom eval for long context, then recommend the winner.
Production deployment of the chosen approach with monitoring for cost and latency, plus documentation for your team on when to switch strategies as models evolve.

faq-item.faq-q: When should I choose RAG over long context windows?
faq-item.faq-a: Choose RAG when you need cost efficiency at scale (long context costs grow linearly with token count), real-time data freshness (RAG queries live databases), or when your documents exceed 1 million tokens—long context models become prohibitively expensive and slow at that scale.

faq-item.faq-q: Are long context windows accurate enough to replace RAG?
faq-item.faq-a: In 2026, models like Gemini 1.5 Pro and GPT-4-128k show strong retrieval accuracy within 200k tokens, but accuracy degrades beyond that and costs can be 10x higher per query compared to RAG. For small, static knowledge bases under 100k tokens, long context is viable and simpler.

faq-item.faq-q: Can I use both RAG and long context together?
faq-item.faq-a: Yes, a hybrid pattern is common: use RAG to retrieve the top 10 most relevant chunks, then feed those into a long context window for reasoning. This balances cost and accuracy, and is the approach we recommend for most production systems in 2026.

faq-item.faq-q: How do I estimate the cost difference between RAG and long context?
faq-item.faq-a: For a 1M token corpus with 100 daily queries, RAG costs roughly $0.10–$0.50/day in embeddings and retrieval, while long context costs $5–$20/day in input tokens alone. We provide a detailed cost projection in the architecture comparison phase.
